chapter.li: LEChapter1 Verse1 Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the commandment of God and the Lord Jesus Christ, our Savior and our hope, VerseEnd Verse2 unto Timothy, my own son in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God our Father and Jesus Christ our Lord. VerseEnd

Verse3 I implored you to remain still at Ephesus when I went into Macedonia, that you might charge some that they teach no other doctrine, VerseEnd Verse4 neither give heed to fables and endless genealogies which minister questions, rather than godly edifying, which is in faith — so do. VerseEnd Verse5 Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned VerseEnd — Verse6 from which some, having swerved, have turned aside unto vain conversation, VerseEnd Verse7 desiring to be teachers of the law, understanding neither what they say nor whereof they affirm. VerseEnd

Verse8 But we know that the law is good if a man use it lawfully, VerseEnd Verse9 knowing this: that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and worldly, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, VerseEnd Verse10 for whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for kidnappers, for liars, for perjured people, and if there is any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine VerseEnd Verse11 according to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust. VerseEnd

Verse12 And I thank Christ Jesus our Lord who has enabled me, for he counted me faithful, putting me into the ministry, VerseEnd Verse13 who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious; but I obtained mercy because I did it ignorantly in unbelief. VerseEnd Verse14 And the grace of our Lord was exceedingly abundant with faith and love, which is in Christ Jesus. VerseEnd Verse15 This is a faithful saying and worthy of all acceptance: that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am chief. VerseEnd Verse16 Nevertheless, for this cause I obtained mercy: that in me first, Jesus Christ might show forth all long-suffering for a pattern to them who should hereafter believe on him to life everlasting. VerseEnd Verse17 Now unto the king — eternal, immortal, invisible, the only wise God — be honor and glory for ever and ever. Amen. VerseEnd

Verse18 This charge I commit unto you, son Timothy, according to the prophecies which went before on you, that you by them might war a good warfare, VerseEnd Verse19 holding faith and a good conscience — which some, having put away concerning faith, have made shipwreck, VerseEnd Verse20 of whom is Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I have delivered unto Satan that they may learn not to blaspheme. VerseEnd

LEChapter2 Verse1 I exhort therefore that first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men, VerseEnd Verse2 for kings and for all that are in authority, that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and dignity. VerseEnd Verse3 For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Savior, VerseEnd Verse4 who is desirous to have all men saved and come unto the knowledge of the truth which is in Christ Jesus, VerseEnd Verse5 who is the only begotten Son of God and ordained to be a mediator between God and man, who is one God and has power over all men, VerseEnd Verse6 who gave himself a ransom for all, to be testified in due time, VerseEnd Verse7 for which I am ordained a preacher and an apostle — I speak the truth in Christ, and lie not — a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth. VerseEnd

Verse8 I desire therefore that men pray everywhere, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting VerseEnd — Verse9 in like manner also, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with modesty and sobriety, not with braided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly apparel, VerseEnd Verse10 but which becomes women professing godliness with good works. VerseEnd Verse11 Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection, VerseEnd Verse12 for I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence. VerseEnd Verse13 For Adam was first formed, then Eve. VerseEnd Verse14 And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression. VerseEnd Verse15 Notwithstanding, they shall be saved in childbearing if they continue in faith, and charity, and holiness, with sobriety. VerseEnd

LEChapter3 Verse1 This is a true saying: If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desires a good work. VerseEnd Verse2 A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behavior, given to hospitality, apt to teach, VerseEnd Verse3 not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy money, but patient, not a brawler, not covetous, VerseEnd Verse4 one that rules well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity VerseEnd — Verse5 for, if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God? VerseEnd — Verse6 not a recent convert, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil. VerseEnd Verse7 Moreover, he must have a good report of them who are outside, lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil. VerseEnd Verse8 Likewise, the deacons must be grave, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy money, VerseEnd Verse9 holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience. VerseEnd Verse10 And let these also first be proved; then, let them use the office of a deacon, being found blameless. VerseEnd Verse11 Even so must their wives be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things. VerseEnd Verse12 Let the deacons be the husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well, VerseEnd Verse13 for they that have used the office of a deacon well acquire to themselves a good degree and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus. VerseEnd

Verse14 These things write I unto you, hoping to come unto you shortly, VerseEnd Verse15 but if I delay long, that you may know how you ought to behave yourself in the House of God, which is the church of the living God. The pillar and ground of the truth VerseEnd Verse16 is — and without controversy, great is the mystery of godliness — God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory. VerseEnd

LEChapter4 Verse1 Now the spirit speaks expressly that in the latter times, some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits and doctrines of devils, VerseEnd Verse2 speaking lies in hypocrisy, having their conscience seared as with a hot iron, VerseEnd Verse3 forbidding to marry and commanding to abstain from foods which God has created to be received with thanksgiving of them who believe and know the truth. VerseEnd Verse4 For every creation of God is good and nothing to be refused if it is received with thanksgiving, VerseEnd Verse5 for it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer. VerseEnd

Verse6 If you put the brethren in remembrance of these things, you shall be a good minister of Jesus Christ, nourished up in the words of faith and of good doctrine unto which you have attained. VerseEnd Verse7 But refuse worldly and old wives’ fables, and exercise yourself rather unto godliness, VerseEnd Verse8 for bodily exercise profits little, but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is and of that which is to come. VerseEnd Verse9 This is a faithful saying and worthy of all acceptance. VerseEnd Verse10 For that is why we both labor and suffer reproach — because we trust in the living God, who is the Savior of all men, especially of those that believe. VerseEnd Verse11 These things command and teach. VerseEnd

Verse12 Let no man despise your youth, but be an example of the believers — in word, in conduct, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity. VerseEnd Verse13 Until I come, give heed to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine. VerseEnd Verse14 Neglect not the gift that is in you, which was given you by prophecy with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery. VerseEnd Verse15 Meditate upon these things; give yourself wholly to them, that your progress may appear to all. VerseEnd Verse16 Take heed unto yourself and unto the doctrine; continue in them, for in doing this, you shall both save yourself and them that hear you. VerseEnd

LEChapter5 Verse1 Rebuke not an elder, but entreat him as a father, and the younger men as brethren, VerseEnd Verse2 the elder women as mothers, the younger as sisters, with all purity. VerseEnd Verse3 Honor widows that are widows indeed; VerseEnd Verse4 but if any widow have children or grandchildren, let them learn first to show piety at home and to requite their parents, for that is good and acceptable before God. VerseEnd Verse5 Now she that is a widow indeed, and desolate, trusts in God and continues in supplications and prayers night and day. VerseEnd Verse6 But she that lives in pleasure is dead while she lives. VerseEnd Verse7 And these things give in charge, that they may be blameless. VerseEnd Verse8 But if any provide not for his own, and especially for those of his own house, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever. VerseEnd

Verse9 Let not a widow be taken into the number under sixty years old, having been the wife of one man, VerseEnd Verse10 well-reported of for good works, if she have brought up children, if she have lodged strangers, if she have washed the saints’ clothes, if she have relieved the afflicted, if she have diligently followed every good work. VerseEnd Verse11 But the younger widows refuse, for when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry, VerseEnd Verse12 having damnation because they have cast off their first faith. VerseEnd Verse13 And at the same time, they learn to be idle, wandering about from house to house — and not only idle, but tattlers also and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not. VerseEnd Verse14 I desire therefore that the younger women marry, bear children, guide the house. Give no opportunity to the adversary to speak reproachfully, VerseEnd Verse15 for some are already turned aside after Satan. VerseEnd Verse16 If any man or woman that believes has widows, let them relieve them, and let not the church be burdened, that it may relieve them that are widows indeed. VerseEnd

Verse17 Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honor, especially they who labor in the word and doctrine; VerseEnd Verse18 for the scripture says, You shall not muzzle the ox that treads out the grain, and, The laborer is worthy of his reward. VerseEnd Verse19 Against an elder receive not an accusation, but before two or three witnesses. VerseEnd Verse20 Them that sin, rebuke before all, that others also may fear. VerseEnd Verse21 I charge you before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the elect angels, that you observe these things without preferring one before another, doing nothing by partiality. VerseEnd Verse22 Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other men’s sins. Keep yourself pure. VerseEnd Verse24 Some men’s sins are open beforehand, going before to judgment, and some men, they follow after. VerseEnd Verse25 Likewise also, the good works of some are manifest beforehand, and they that are otherwise cannot be hidden. VerseEnd Verse23 Drink no longer water, but use a little wine for your stomach’s sake and your often infirmities. VerseEnd

LEChapter6 Verse1 Let as many servants as are under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honor, that the name of God and his doctrine are not blasphemed. VerseEnd Verse2 And they that have believing masters, let them not despise them because they are brethren, but rather do them service because they are faithful and beloved partakers of the benefit. These things teach and exhort. VerseEnd Verse3 If any man teach otherwise and consent not to wholesome words, even the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which is according to godliness, VerseEnd Verse4 he is proud, knowing nothing, but doting about questions and strifes of words, whereof comes envy, strife, railings, evil surmisings, VerseEnd Verse5 perverse disputings of men of corrupt minds and destitute of the truth, supposing that gain is godliness. From such, withdraw yourself. VerseEnd Verse6 But godliness with contentment is great gain, VerseEnd Verse7 for we brought nothing into this world and it is certain we can carry nothing out. VerseEnd Verse8 And having food and raiment, let us be with them content. VerseEnd Verse9 But they that will be rich fall into temptation, and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition. VerseEnd Verse10 For the love of money is the root of all evil, which while some coveted after they have erred from the faith and pierced themselves through with many sorrows. VerseEnd

Verse11 But you, O man of God, flee these things and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness. VerseEnd Verse12 Fight the good fight of faith; lay hold on eternal life, unto which you are also called and have professed a good profession before many witnesses. VerseEnd Verse13 I give you charge in the sight of God, who quickens all things, and before Christ Jesus, who before Pontius Pilate witnessed a good confession, VerseEnd Verse14 that you keep this commandment without spot, irreproachable, until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ, VerseEnd Verse15 which in his times he shall show, who is the blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings and Lord of lords; VerseEnd Verse16 to whom be honor and power everlasting; who only has immortality, dwelling in the light; whom no man has seen nor can see, unto whom no man can approach — only he who has the light and the hope of immortality dwelling in him. VerseEnd

Verse17 Charge them that are rich in this world that they be not haughty, nor trust in uncertain riches but in the living God, who gives us richly all things to enjoy, VerseEnd Verse18 that they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to share, VerseEnd Verse19 laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold on eternal life. VerseEnd

Verse20 O Timothy, keep that which is committed to your trust, avoiding worldly and vain babblings and oppositions of science falsely so called, VerseEnd Verse21 which some professing have erred concerning the faith. Grace be with you. Amen. VerseEnd

p.i: The first to Timothy was written from Laodicea, which is the chiefest city of Phrygia Pacatiana.
